questions.prompt: Use Trials 1 and 3 as evidence. Name the one variable that changed and the variables held constant, report both lifting results, and explain what the iron core does to the field and why the measured current stayed the same.
questions.rubricText:
@[Always] Grading feedback: Evidence must compare the recorded Trial 1 and Trial 3 results. BusyBee scoring: Award points only in 0.5-point increments, including whole points, from 0 to the question maximum. Select a rubric-supported allowed score; never report hundredths such as 2.85/3. Do not average or percentage-scale rubric criteria into an off-grid score. A binary completion rubric still permits only 0 or full credit. Allowed scores for this question: 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2.
a. Full credit: Identifies core material as the only changed variable, names the controls, reports 49 and 4 clips, explains that iron concentrates the field, and explains that current stayed the same because the electrical resistance and voltage were unchanged. Partial credit: Gives the correct pattern but omits data, controls, or the current explanation. No credit: Compares uncontrolled trials or claims the iron core caused the current change.

questions.prompt: Defend the design with your highest strength-to-cost ratio. Compare at least three different tested designs, giving each design's turns, core, diameter, cells, wiring, clips lifted, cost, and calculated clips / cost to 2 decimals. Explain how the comparison supports your choice. If the design must lift at least 190 clips, would you keep your best-value design or choose a different one? Use measured results to justify the tradeoff. Explain why maximizing lifting strength alone can give worse value. State whether you reached the 6.38 clips-per-cost target and support your conclusion with your checked results.
questions.rubricText:
@[Always] Grading feedback: Grade the evidence-based comparison of three tested designs and reasoning about the new 190-clip requirement. Checked ratios are supporting evidence, not an independent calculation assessment. Several designs can share the same score rounded to 2 decimals. BusyBee scoring: Award points only in 0.5-point increments, including whole points, from 0 to the question maximum. Select a rubric-supported allowed score; never report hundredths such as 2.85/3. Do not average or percentage-scale rubric criteria into an off-grid score. A binary completion rubric still permits only 0 or full credit. Allowed scores for this question: 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3.
a. Full credit: Compares at least three complete tested designs with accurate clips, costs, and calculated ratios; identifies the best ratio; correctly explains whether the best-value design meets the 190-clip requirement and selects a qualifying tested alternative or proposes another test if none qualifies; and explains a specific strength-versus-cost tradeoff. Partial credit: Correct method or useful comparisons but missing a design, evidence for the new requirement, or tradeoff explanation. No credit: Gives no usable calculations or selects a winner solely by clip count without considering cost.
